title: VST’s view of the Leo Triplet and beyond
caption: The Leo Triplet and surrounding field, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: Leo Triplet · constellation Leo · about 35 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Three bright galaxies in Leo, the Lion, sit in this wide view, surrounded by a crowd of fainter objects. Some of those fainter points are distant galaxies far in the background, while others are much closer stars in our own Milky Way.

The trio is known as the Leo Triplet, a group of interacting galaxies about 35 million light-years away. It was made with the VLT Survey Telescope and its OmegaCAM camera, a pairing well suited to wide surveys.

Survey telescopes like this one cover large areas of sky at once. That makes them good at mapping the Universe beyond our galaxy, and at picking up very faint, low-brightness structures in the Milky Way's halo, the sparse region of stars that surrounds its disc. A single frame like this holds nearby stars, galaxies in the middle distance and faint galaxies far beyond.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (51.72 x 41.86 arcminutes) and distance (35 million light years), the frame spans roughly 527,000 × 426,000 light-years. Its light set out about 35 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This composite comes from the OmegaCAM camera on the VLT Survey Telescope. Light through a near-infrared filter is coloured red, light from the red part of the spectrum is coloured green, and green light is coloured magenta.
filters: 480 nm · Optical G (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Optical R (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
770 nm · Infrared I (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: The colours are shifted from their real hues, and the near-infrared part of the data is invisible to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image is a composite of exposures through three different filters, each given its own colour so that the combined picture shows how the scene looks across visible and near-infrared light.
alt: Three bright galaxies surrounded by many faint background galaxies and foreground stars.
